newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Soviet flag provokes punches in Ukraine parliament.
newsitem.headline: Soviet flag provokes punches in Ukraine parliament.

text.p: Punches flew in the Ukrainian parliament on Thursday after a communist deputy raised the hammer and sickle to commemorate the signing of Josef Stalin's constitution 60 years ago.

"Dozens of deputies went in to seize the flag and rip it up. Several communists tried to defend it, so it is not surprising that people got punched as a result," right-winger Mykola Porovsky, who heads the Republican Party, told Reuters.

In the fracas in the Kiev parliament, one deputy hurled the red Soviet flag to the ground and Porovsky grabbed it and ripped it to shreds. Witnesses said up to 20 deputies were involved in the confrontation.

"The communist swarm raised the red flag. This caused justifiable indignation from several factions. We perceived this as an insult to the memory of millions of Ukrainians who died in Stalin's repressions," Porovsky said.
Communist leader Volodymyr Moysenko had planted the Soviet symbol at his seat before giving a five-minute speech denouncing Ukraine's first post-independence constitution signed this year.
"Today we all remember the great Soviet constitutional holiday. The workers reject the June 28 constitution," he said.

"Stop talking! Your speech is on the brink of breaking the law!" said speaker Olexander Moroz, head of the socialist faction. A radio live broadcast of the session was interrupted and witnesses said it was at that point a fight broke out.

The communists, who yearn for the Soviet Union and believe Kiev should re-build a union with Moscow, were commemorating the day the 1936 Soviet constitution was signed, giving the Communist Party unlimited power.
But other parties in parliament treasure Ukraine's independence from Moscow, won in 1991 and set in stone in the country's first constitution signed this summer.
Millions of Ukrainians starved under Stalin's collectivisation and deportation programmes in the 1930s.
"By 1937, millions of Ukrainians had starved to death. Yet today the communists' descendants are raising the flag on the Ukrainian parliament? It's a provocation!" Porovsky declared.
It was not the first time a flag was destroyed in a parliament on former Soviet territory.

Three ultra-nationalist deputies from Ukraine's rightist UNA-UNSO movement ripped up a Russian tricolour in the chamber days after a right-wing deputy destroyed a Ukrainian flag in the Russian parliament last year.
Russia and Ukrain have been arguing over several issues since the Soviet Union broke up, particularly about the division of the Black Sea Fleet based on Ukrainian territory.
